decision: Require explicit scenario coverage in addition to zero-error counters before REAL-WORKER READY
problem: A campaign could previously report zero duplicate mutations, zero unresolved requests, and zero QA-before-join without actually exercising retry/reconciliation or the QA join barrier. Absence of observed failure is weaker than evidence that the failure mode was tested.

independent_reviews.correctness: weak: unexercised scenarios look identical to successful scenarios
independent_reviews.qa: existing tests pass but cannot prove scenario coverage

independent_reviews.approach: Explicit raw-event scenario coverage gate composed with the existing collector/readiness gate
independent_reviews.correctness: strong: requires framing, mutation, pending-to-resolved reconciliation, recovery, QA join, stale-token probe, and current-token completion
independent_reviews.robustness: fail-closed on missing evidence while preserving existing provenance/topology/latency checks
independent_reviews.latency: no extra qrexec calls; one linear in-memory pass over campaign events
independent_reviews.resource_use: O(n) time and bounded request-id sets for a bounded campaign
independent_reviews.regression_risk: low: additive release gate; production coordinator and worker semantics unchanged
independent_reviews.qa: new positive and omission tests cover every required scenario

independent_reviews.approach: External telemetry/attestation service decides campaign completeness
independent_reviews.robustness: adds another distributed dependency and key/service lifecycle
independent_reviews.regression_risk: larger operational and security surface before Qubes execution is proven
independent_reviews.qa: would require service lifecycle and failure-mode tests

why: It closes a concrete false-readiness path without changing production behavior or adding distributed infrastructure.
failures_and_lessons: A zero counter proves only that a failure was not observed; it does not prove the corresponding fault path was exercised.
Release evidence should bind both outcome invariants and scenario coverage.
Cryptographic/dom0 attestation remains a later hardening step; this change addresses completeness, not trust-root provenance.
safety: Synthetic/defensive Qubes validation only. No real financial transactions or external side effects.
